activity.source: Sigma-Aldrich A3176 alpha-amylase (porcine pancreas, Type VI-B): 1 U liberates 1.0 mg maltose from starch in 3 min at pH 6.9, 20 °C; ≥5 U/mg solid

heat_inactivation.applied: only above T_opt (falling limb); none claimed at or below T_opt
heat_inactivation.source: Miłek, Molecules 26 (2021) 4117, doi:10.3390/molecules26144117, Table 1 row 1a (Sigma porcine pancreatic α-amylase, data of Akhond et al. 2016, doi:10.1007/s12010-016-2145-1): first-order deactivation, T_opt 311.06 K, E_d 164.9 kJ/mol, β 1.46, t_a 3 min
heat_inactivation.corroboration: Singh, Shandilya, Kundu, Kayastha, PLoS ONE 10 (2015) e0129203, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0129203, Fig 3A: WHEAT alpha-amylase unperturbed to 65 C, 4% loss at 70 C, complete loss around 85 C (different organism; not used as a constant)
heat_inactivation.state: Vessel::amylase_inactive_moles (irreversible; not carried by a pour)

native_granules.gelatinisation_source: Belitz, Grosch, Schieberle, Food Chemistry, 3rd ed., Springer 2004, pp. 318-323 (ISBN 3-540-40818-5): unmodified native starches start swelling at 55 °C (some types) to 85 °C (others); value as quoted by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starch_gelatinization
native_granules.granule_rate_source: Slaughter, Ellis, Butterworth, Biochim. Biophys. Acta 1525 (2001) 29-36, doi:10.1016/S0304-4165(00)00162-8: gelatinisation raises porcine pancreatic α-amylase k_cat/K_m 13-fold (waxy rice) to 239-fold (potato); source-dependent, so no generic granule rate
native_granules.rule: plain `starch` (no material recipe; generic laboratory starch of unstated plant source, insoluble in the registry) booked as gelatinised (held in liquid water at >= GELATINISED_AT_K during a clock step) is digested at the soluble-starch A3176 unit rate; plain native or retrograded starch is refused; starch from a material recipe follows the digestibility table
native_granules.state: Vessel::starch_gelatinised_moles (re-gelatinised by >= 85 C) and Vessel::starch_digestion (retrograded pool, 4 C hold seconds, table clock, digested per lot source); not carried by a pour
native_granules.product: booked as maltose equivalents (the unit counts reducing sugar as maltose); maltose, maltotriose and alpha-limit dextrins split NOT modelled: no sourced split (typed note not-modeled.amylase-starch-product-split-unsourced)

digestibility.protocol: protocol W: 4 U Sigma A3176 porcine pancreatic alpha-amylase + 4 U A. niger amyloglucosidase (Megazyme E-AMGDF) per 10 mg starch, pH 6.0 phosphate, 37 C; RDS = digested by 20 min, SDS = 20-120 min, RS = rest
digestibility.window: 37 C +/- 0.5 K and 0.5x-2x the protocol dose (A3176 at the >=5 U/mg lower specification); outside: not-modeled.amylase-starch-outside-source-protocol (no sourced dose or temperature law)
digestibility.time_course: piecewise linear through (0,0), (20 min, RDS), (120 min, 100-RS), applied as a conditional fraction of what is left; nothing claimed after 120 min (not-modeled.amylase-starch-beyond-source-time); ranges use the lower digested end
digestibility.retrogradation: gelatinised starch held in liquid water at 4 C for a cumulative 36 h (the cited tables' treatment) is booked retrograded; >= 85 C re-gelatinises it
digestibility.caveat: tabulated values include amyloglucosidase, which acts synergistically on granules; amylase alone is expected to digest no faster, so booked digestion is an upper-bound-like figure
digestibility.products: maltose equivalents; alpha-amylase gives maltose, maltotriose (minor maltotetraose) and alpha-limit dextrins (PLoS One 8 (2013) e59745, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0059745); split unsourced, typed note not-modeled.amylase-starch-product-split-unsourced
digestibility.iodine: the starch-iodine complex reads remaining ledger starch (starch_iodine::complex_moles)

starch_iodine_optics.reason: Pesek et al., Molecules 27 (2022) 8974, doi:10.3390/molecules27248974, sect. 2.1: 'reliable extinction coefficients for the amylose-iodine-iodide complex are not known'. The blue-value assay (Corn Refiners Association AMYLO.01, 620 nm) calibrates against amylose standards rather than an epsilon. No value was found that could be cited. Retried 2026-11-11: Pesek & Silaghi-Dumitrescu, Molecules 29 (2024) 641, doi:10.3390/molecules29030641 (full text) gives no coefficient; Knutson, Carbohydr. Polym. 42 (2000) 65, doi:10.1016/S0144-8617(99)00126-5 and Abe, Bull. Chem. Soc. Jpn. 31 (1958) 661, doi:10.1246/bcsj.31.661 are paywalled (not read); open analytical papers report APPARENT absorptivities per iodide/iodine of 4e4 to 6e5 L/(mol cm) that depend on starch source, amylose fraction and excess-starch conditions, so none transfers to a generic 'starch' whose amylose fraction the bench does not know.
starch_iodine_optics.still_read: free I2 and I3- from their cited epsilon values (iodine_chemistry)
